title: Ghormeh Sabzi
subtitle: Persian herb and lamb stew
excerpt: A deeply savoury, herb-dominant Persian stew of slow-cooked lamb shoulder and kidney beans in a broth built on finely fried fresh herbs and a tang of tamarind. One of Iran's most beloved national dishes, it requires patience but very little skill.
sourceNotes: Ghormeh sabzi is considered one of the oldest Persian dishes, with roots going back over a thousand years. The name translates roughly as 'fried herbs'. The defining characteristic is the large quantity of finely chopped fresh herbs fried in oil until very dark, which concentrates their flavour and gives the stew its distinctive deep green colour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well for up to 3 months. The flavour actually improves after freezing and reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a large pot. Ideal for batch cooking as it only gets better with time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes significantly better made a day ahead. Make the day before and reheat gently.

content.text: The most important step is frying the herbs. They need to cook in oil in a separate pan for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until they are very dark and aromatic and have reduced dramatically in volume. Skipping this step or rushing it will give you a stew that tastes of raw herbs rather than the complex, concentrated flavour that defines ghormeh sabzi. Traditional versions use dried fenugreek leaves, which you can find in Middle Eastern and South Asian grocery stores; this recipe substitutes cumin for a similar earthy note.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the chopped parsley, coriander, spinach, spring onion, and leek. Fry, stirring often, for 15 to 20 minutes until very dark green, dry, and deeply aromatic. Set aside.
In the stockpot, heat the remaining olive oil over a high heat. Brown the lamb pieces in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until well coloured. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, turmeric, and cumin and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot. Add the fried herbs, stock, and tamarind paste. Stir to combine. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on a low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the kidney beans and cook for a further 30 minutes until the lamb is falling-tender and the stew is dark and rich. Season generously with salt.
Serve over saffron basmati rice, with pickles on the side if you have them.

items.symptom: Stew tastes of raw greens rather than deep herbs.
items.cause: The herbs were not fried long enough or at high enough heat.
items.fix: Fry herbs in oil for a full 20 minutes until very dark and dry.

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The heat was too low to properly braise the shoulder.
items.fix: Ensure a steady, gentle simmer; add 30 more minutes if needed.

items.cause: Too much tamarind paste was used.
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar and simmer for 10 more minutes to balance.
